script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'review-mainsolver-enum',
  description: 'Adversarially review the main-solver LIA* enumeration implementation',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'three lenses: soundness, termination/progress, mechanics' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial verification of findings' },
  ],
}

const FINDINGS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string' },
          detail: { type: 'string' },
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'major', 'minor'] },
        },
        required: ['title', 'detail', 'severity'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['findings'],
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: { isReal: { type: 'boolean' }, reasoning: { type: 'string' } },
  required: ['isReal', 'reasoning'],
}

const CTX = `Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5, branch lazy). Uncommitted changes: run
"git diff" there. New feature: option arith-liastar-main-solver moves the lazy LIA* cell
enumeration from a per-lambda subsolver into the MAIN solver. Design (see MainEnum in
src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h and mainSolverCheckStar/advanceStage/
emitDriverLemma/getModelDisjunct/getMainEnum/addEnumLemma in liastar_extension.cpp):
- lambda bound vars -> fresh integer skolems y; base(y) = predicate (ites/nots removed) + y>=0.
- Stage guards: h_0 => base(y); per discovered cone-disjunct D_k a fresh h_k with
  h_k => h_{k-1} and h_k => not(D_k(y)); en.guard is the current h_k; each h is
  ensureLiteral'd and preferPhase'd true. h_0 additionally gets a split lemma.
- Driver lemma per (literal, stage): literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k), unguarded,
  where star_k = d_lastStarLia[literal] (under-approximation built by processDisjunct)
  and p[v] is the vector predicate. Claimed satisfiability-preserving.
- Each full-effort round: catch up stages for cones discovered via other literals; if
  guard fixed false at level 0 (Valuation::isFixed) -> emit exact equivalence
  (processDisjunct complete=true); if guard true in SAT assignment -> read the cell from
  arithModel via getModelDisjunct (substitute+rewrite each atom of base; equality atoms
  false in model become strict inequalities; skolems missing from arithModel fall back to
  TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue), dedupe against d_lazyCones, advanceStage, then
  processDisjunct(false) emits the guarded equivalence g_k => (literal = star_k) and
  deactivates the previous g; then emitDriverLemma for the new stage.
- Tests: all 9 regress1/arith/liastar tests pass in this mode (Debug), and in the other
  three modes (accumulate/push-pop/eager); unit test passes.
Focus ONLY on problems introduced by the new main-solver mode (not pre-existing issues in
the subsolver paths). Report findings with concrete code references.`

const LENSES = [
  {
    key: 'soundness',
    prompt: `${CTX}
Lens: logical soundness. Questions to attack:
1. Is the driver lemma literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k) really satisfiability-preserving in
   ALL cases -- including stale drivers from earlier stages (each stage's driver stays asserted
   forever, with its own h_j whose constraint set is frozen at stage j)? Construct a
   countermodel if possible.
2. Is the completeness conclusion from Valuation::isFixed(guard)=false sound? isFixed means
   implied by input assertions -- but the implication chain includes liastar's own lemmas
   (drivers, guarded equivalences, star constraints). Could not(h_k) be fixed for a reason
   OTHER than base-and-negated-disjuncts being unsat (e.g. via the driver and a fixed
   not(literal)), making the exact equivalence emission wrong?
3. getModelDisjunct: the disjunct fixes every atom of base; equality-false becomes GT/LT.
   Any way it returns a conjunction NOT implying base (so the cone overcovers) or one not
   containing the model point?
4. Interaction of d_lastStarLia / d_lastGuard between modes or multiple literals sharing a
   lambda: cross-contamination?`,
  },
  {
    key: 'termination-progress',
    prompt: `${CTX}
Lens: termination and progress. Questions to attack:
1. Can the procedure livelock: rounds where guard is false-but-not-fixed and the driver for the
   current stage was already emitted -- emitDriverLemma returns without queueing anything and
   doPendingLemmas sends nothing. Is there a scenario where the solver then answers sat with an
   unjustified positively-asserted literal, or loops forever without progress?
2. Duplicate-cell handling: when the model re-exhibits a known cell, the round emits at most a
   driver. Can this repeat indefinitely (same cell each round)? Note the stage that negates the
   cell was opened in the round that first harvested it -- is en.negated maintained consistently
   with d_lazyCones in ALL paths (addCone drops empty cones!)?
3. advanceStage in the catch-up loop vs processDisjunct ordering: en.negated = pairs.size() is
   executed twice in the harvest path (before/after processDisjunct). Off-by-one risks?
4. incremental mode (push/pop of the main solver between check-sats): lemmas/d_mainEnums/
   d_lastDriver are non-context state; what breaks (e.g. simple.smt2 has two check-sats)?`,
  },
  {
    key: 'mechanics',
    prompt: `${CTX}
Lens: cvc5 mechanics. Questions to attack:
1. ensureLiteral + preferPhase during a full-effort check: legal at that point? (compare the
   existing liastarGuard pattern). Any issue calling them per stage (many stages)?
2. addEnumLemma skips lemmas that rewrite to constants -- could skipping h_k => not(D_k) (if it
   ever rewrites to true) silently break the stage invariant?
3. getModelDisjunct's use of arithModel keys: substitution with non-leaf keys (the arith model
   map can contain non-variable terms); is substitute() over atom nodes safe/correct here?
4. TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue fallback: legal for skolems unknown to the linear solver?
5. Lemma flushing: every path in mainSolverCheckStar ends in doPendingLemmas or processDisjunct
   (which calls it) -- verify, including the early-return paths in checkFullEffort around the
   model-value shortcut.
6. The unused 'seeded' warning, unused includes, style of the new code vs file conventions.`,
  },
]

const results = await pipeline(
  LENSES,
  l => agent(l.prompt, { label: `review:${l.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA }),
  (review, lens) => parallel((review?.findings ?? []).map(f => () =>
    agent(`${CTX}
A reviewer (lens ${lens.key}) claims:
Title: ${f.title}
Detail: ${f.detail}
Adversarially verify against the actual code (git diff + files). Is this a REAL problem
introduced by the new main-solver mode? Default isReal=false unless the reasoning reproduces
concretely from the code.`,
      { label: `verify:${f.title.slice(0, 30)}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA })
      .then(v => ({ ...f, lens: lens.key, verdict: v }))
  ))
)

const all = results.filter(Boolean).flat().filter(Boolean)
return {
  confirmed: all.filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal),
  rejected: all.filter(f => !f.verdict?.isReal).map(f => f.title),
}

confirmed.title: Driver lemma omits the star under-approximation, refuting literals true via the empty sum (confirmed wrong UNSAT)
confirmed.detail: emitDriverLemma (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1026-1034) adds the star disjunct only if d_lastStarLia contains the literal. On the first round (the !seeded path at :1072-1080) and on any round before processDisjunct has run for that literal, the emitted lemma is `literal => (p[v] OR h_k)` with no star disjunct. This is NOT satisfiability-preserving: the zero vector is always in S* (empty sum) but need not satisfy p[v], and h_k dies permanently once base AND negated disjuncts becomes unsat (every driver stays asserted forever). Minimal trigger: a lambda whose predicate is unsatisfiable over the nonnegative orthant and a vector forced to zero by non-unit constraints (the constant-zero case is masked by rewriteStarContains in src/theory/arith/arith_rewriter.cpp:1087). CONFIRMED: with `(declare-const a Int)(declare-const b Int)(assert (>= a 0))(assert (<= a 0))(assert (>= b 0))(assert (<= b 0))(assert (int.star-contains (lambda ((x Int)(y Int)) (and (>= (+ x y) 1) (>= (* (- 1) (+ x y)) 0))) a b))(check-sat)` — eager, lazy-subsolver and push-pop all answer sat; `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-main-solver` answers unsat. The `-o lemmas` dump shows the mechanism exactly: `(lemma (not liastarEnumGuard_4))` (h_0 => base with base rewritten to false) plus the driver `L => (p[v] or liastarEnumGuard_4)` forces not(L). Note the later exact equivalence L = (v=0) from the isFixed branch does not repair this, because the bogus driver remains asserted. Fix direction: when d_lastStarLia has no entry, the driver must still include the trivial under-approximation `v = 0` (and in general a star disjunct current with the guard's stage).

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL. Reproduced end-to-end on a freshly rebuilt binary from the current working tree (ninja cvc5-bin in /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir/build, then re-ran).

1. Reproduction: with the reviewer's test (adjusted only to use (set-logic HO_ALL), required by the parser for lambda), `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-main-solver` answers UNSAT while default/eager, `--arith-liastar-lazy` (subsolver, also under --check-models), and `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-push-pop` all answer SAT. Semantically SAT is correct: the predicate (x+y>=1 AND -(x+y)>=0) is unsatisfiable, so the star set is exactly {0} (empty sum), and a=b=0 satisfies all assertions.

2. Code mechanism matches exactly. In src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp, emitDriverLemma (lines 1008-1037) adds the star branch only conditionally: `auto starIt = d_lastStarLia.find(literal);` (line 1028) with `branches.push_back(starIt->second)` only if found (line 1031). On the first round, mainSolverCheckStar takes the `!seeded` path (lines 1072-1080) and calls emitDriverLemma before processDisjunct has ever run for the literal, so d_lastStarLia has no entry and the emitted lemma is `literal => (p[v] OR h_0)` with no star disjunct. The lemma is queued unguarded and permanently via addEnumLemma -> d_im.addPendingLemma (lines 886-896, 1034).

3. The `-o lemmas` dump shows precisely the claimed two lemmas before the unsat: `(lemma (not liastarEnumGuard_4) :source ARITH_LIA_STAR_ENUM)` (this is h_0 => base from line 882, with base rewritten to false since the predicate is contradictory) and the driver `(=> (int.star-contains ...) (or (and (>= (+ a b) 1) (not (>= (+ a b) 1))) liastarEnumGuard_4))`. p[v] rewrites to false and the guard is fixed false at level 0, so not(literal) is forced against the asserted literal -> wrong UNSAT. Notably the run conflicts out before the isFixed/processDisjunct(complete=true) repair branch (liastar_extension.cpp:1088-1093) even fires; and even if it did, the bogus driver lemma remains asserted, so the exact equivalence literal = (v=0) would just produce the same conflict.

4. The masking detail is also accurate: rewriteStarContains (src/theory/arith/arith_rewriter.cpp:1087-1102) rewrites star-contains to true when all vector elements are constant zero, which is why the trigger needs the vector forced to zero via (>= a 0)/(<= a 0) constraints rather than literal constants.

5. Introduced by the new mode: the entire driver path is reached only under `options().arith.arithLiaStarMainSolver` (liastar_extension.cpp:405-407); the subsolver paths are unaffected.

The not-sat-preserving argument is sound: 0 is always in S* (empty sum), so `literal => (p[v] OR star_k OR h_k)` is only valid when star_k includes at least v=0; omitting it makes the lemma refute literals whose only witness is the empty (or any not-yet-discovered) sum once h_k is dead. The suggested fix direction (always include at least the trivial under-approximation v=0 in the driver when d_lastStarLia has no entry) is consistent with the design comment at lines 1010-1021, which itself states the lemma should contain the star branch.

confirmed.title: Re-harvest dedup compares the raw model disjunct against normalized stored nodes, so it rarely matches
confirmed.detail: mainSolverCheckStar's dedup loop (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) compares the freshly built disjunct from getModelDisjunct — which contains raw `(not atom)` literals for false non-equality atoms (:967) — against d_lazyCones[lambda] entries. But the stored node is the result of LiaStarUtils::removeItesAndNots applied in processDisjunct (:1183) before LiaStarUtils::getMatrix (which returns its input node, src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_utils.cpp:883ff) — negations rewritten into positive comparisons. Whenever a cell contains a negated atom, the syntactic comparison misses, the in-flight-lemma race re-harvests the same cell, and addCone appends a duplicate cone plus advanceStage opens a redundant stage. This is not a soundness hole (a duplicated cone contributes the same semigroup, and the duplicate stage re-negates the same cell), but it defeats the stated purpose of the guard and bloats the star constraints; the comparison should be done on removeItesAndNots-normalized nodes on both sides. Related bookkeeping: if addCone drops the harvested cell as an empty cone, `en.negated = pairs.size()` (:1143) undercounts the stages already advanced.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed real (performance/dedup-defeat, not soundness — as the reviewer states). The chain reproduces concretely: (1) getModelDisjunct builds raw negations `atom.notNode()` for false non-equality atoms (liastar_extension.cpp:967) and returns the disjunct in bound-variable space; (2) processDisjunct normalizes via LiaStarUtils::removeItesAndNots (liastar_extension.cpp:1183), whose removeNot (liastar_utils.cpp:439-465) rewrites e.g. (not (>= a b)) -> (< a b); (3) getMatrix returns {constraints, n} with n the normalized input node (liastar_utils.cpp:900/920/932), and addCone stores {pair.second, cone} in d_lazyCones (liastar_extension.cpp:670); (4) the dedup loop (liastar_extension.cpp:1120-1128) compares the raw fresh disjunct against these normalized stored nodes with Node identity, so it can never match any cell containing a false non-equality atom (it only works for all-true cells, and false integer-equality atoms which become positive GT/LT at :962 and survive normalization). On a miss, addCone (no dedup, only empty-cone drop) appends a duplicate cone, getStarConstraints (:695-719) mints redundant fresh skolems/constraints bloating the star under-approximation, and advanceStage opens a redundant stage — defeating the guard's explicitly stated purpose (comment :1118-1119). The race is plausible especially via the getCandidateModelValue fallback (:915-927) whose values need not satisfy the queued stage-negation lemma. All of this is new code introduced by the main-solver mode. Caveats: the side remark that `en.negated = pairs.size()` (:1143) "undercounts" is incorrect — per liastar_extension.h:310-312 `negated` counts negated d_lazyCones entries and the invariant remains consistent if a cone were dropped (and a model-inhabited cell cannot yield an empty cone anyway); and whether the re-harvest race actually fires in the 9 regressions is unverified, so the impact may be latent. The core finding and the proposed fix (compare removeItesAndNots-normalized nodes on both sides) are correct.

confirmed.title: MainEnum state outlives user-context-scoped lemmas: wrong sat after pop in incremental mode (confirmed)
confirmed.detail: All guard-chain lemmas (h_0 => base, h_k => h_{k-1}, h_k => not(D_k), drivers) are sent as ordinary theory lemmas and are RETRACTED on user-context pop, but the bookkeeping that gates their emission lives in non-context-dependent std::maps: d_mainEnums and d_lastDriver (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h:450-462), plus en.negated and en.guard inside MainEnum. getMainEnum only seeds h_0 => base once per lambda lifetime (liastar_extension.cpp:823-884), advanceStage lemmas are emitted once per cone (en.negated never resets), and emitDriverLemma no-ops when d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard. After a pop, en.guard refers to a dangling SAT variable with no chain behind it: the SAT solver can set it true while the skolems sit in an already-covered cell; mainSolverCheckStar then re-harvests a known cell, the dedupe path (liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) re-emits an already-cached driver, doPendingLemmas sends nothing, and the candidate model is accepted. CONFIRMED: /tmp/liastar_pushpop2.smt2 (check (1 1) unsat, pop, then check (2 1) with the same lambda, which is also unsat since 2+1 < 5) answers `unsat` then `sat` in main-solver mode; subsolver mode answers `unsat`/`unsat`. The subsolver mode is immune because its accumulated state lives in the subsolver, not in the main SAT solver's retractable clause database. Note the existing regress test simple.smt2 uses push/pop but masks this because its second query is certified via the p[v] split. Fix direction: make the per-lambda/per-literal gating user-context-dependent (CDO/CDHashMap on userContext()), or re-seed the full chain when the user context changes.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED real. Independently reproduced: /tmp/liastar_pushpop2.smt2 (same lambda as regress simple.smt2; queries (1 1) then, after pop, (2 1), both genuinely unsat since any nonzero star member has coordinate-sum >= 5) answers unsat then SAT under --arith-liastar-main-solver with build/bin/cvc5 (binary at 06:43 today, newer than all modified sources), while default-lazy subsolver, --arith-liastar-push-pop, and eager modes all answer unsat/unsat. Mechanism verified against code: the guard-chain and driver lemmas are ordinary theory lemmas retracted on user-context pop, but their emission gating is non-context-dependent state: d_mainEnums and d_lastDriver are plain std::map (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h:455,462), and en.guard/en.negated live in MainEnum. getMainEnum returns early for a known lambda (liastar_extension.cpp:828-832) so h_0 => base (line 882) is never re-seeded; the catch-up loop (1060-1070) only emits stages for i >= en.negated so the h_k chain is never re-emitted; emitDriverLemma no-ops when d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard (1021-1025). In check 2 the only new lemma is the driver for the new literal, literal => (p[2,1] or h_1), where h_1 is a dangling SAT variable with no chain behind it; the SAT solver sets it true with the skolems in the already-covered cell. The -t liastar-ext trace confirms this: check 2 re-harvests the identical disjunct (and (>= (+ x y) 5) (< (+ x (- y)) 6) (>= x 0) (>= y 0)) already coned in check 1, which is only possible if h_1 => not(D_1) was retracted. mainSolverCheckStar then hits the dedupe path (1120-1128), emitDriverLemma no-ops, doPendingLemmas sends nothing, the round ends lemma-free and the bogus model is accepted as sat. The bug is introduced by the new mode: MainEnum and this whole path are new in the diff, and the subsolver modes are immune because their accumulated negations live in the persistent subsolver engine, not the main solver's retractable clause database. The reviewer's note that regress simple.smt2 masks this is also correct: its post-pop vector (4,4) satisfies p directly, so the p[v] split certifies it without the enumeration chain. Fix direction (user-context-dependent gating, e.g. CDO/CDHashMap on userContext(), or re-seeding the chain on user-context change) is sound.

confirmed.title: Cell dedupe compares raw harvested disjunct against the normalized stored node, so it misses semantically equal cells
confirmed.detail: mainSolverCheckStar's re-harvest guard (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) compares `pair.first == disjunct` where `disjunct` is the raw output of getModelDisjunct (which produces `atom.notNode()` literals for atoms false in the model, liastar_extension.cpp:964-968), while `pair.first` stored in d_lazyCones is the output of `LiaStarUtils::getMatrix(variables, removeItesAndNots(disjunct)).second` (processDisjunct, liastar_extension.cpp:1183-1197; getMatrix returns its input node, liastar_utils.cpp:883-941). Whenever the harvested cell contains at least one negated atom, the raw and stored forms differ syntactically and the dedupe never fires; the same cell is then run through processDisjunct again, appending a duplicate cone and duplicate star skolems/constraints (semantically harmless but bloats the encoding, and the protection the comment claims does not exist). Compare the normalized form instead (apply removeItesAndNots before the comparison), or store the raw form alongside the cone.

verdict.reasoning: Verified concretely against the code. (1) The dedupe in mainSolverCheckStar (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1120-1128, new in the diff) compares `pair.first == disjunct` where `disjunct` is the raw output of getModelDisjunct (line 1109). (2) getModelDisjunct produces `atom.notNode()` for any non-equality atom false in the model (lines 964-968; integer equalities are special-cased to GT/LT at 948-962), so most harvested cells contain NOT literals. (3) The stored `pair.first` in d_lazyCones is the normalized node: processDisjunct applies removeItesAndNots (line 1183) before getMatrix (line 1188), getMatrix returns its input node as pair.second (liastar_utils.cpp:900/920/932), and addCone stores pair.second (liastar_extension.cpp:670). removeNot rewrites e.g. (not (>= a b)) to (< a b) (liastar_utils.cpp:446-465), so raw and stored forms differ syntactically whenever the cell has a negated atom, and the dedupe never fires for such cells; it can only ever match the all-positive cell. (4) On a miss, the code re-runs advanceStage + processDisjunct: addCone appends a duplicate cone unconditionally (650-671) and getStarConstraints mints duplicate fresh skolems/constraints (693-712) — encoding bloat, not unsoundness, exactly as claimed. Severity caveat: the dedupe is a defensive guard for a narrow timing window (model produced before the negation lemma took effect); in steady state advanceStage's eager guard replacement plus the persisted h_new => not(D) lemma prevent re-harvest, so the broken comparison rarely matters in practice. But within the window the comment's claimed protection genuinely does not exist for any cell with a negated atom, all the reviewer's line references check out, and the suggested fix (normalize before comparing, or store the raw form) is correct. Real but low-severity defect introduced by the new main-solver mode.

confirmed.title: getCandidateModelValue fallback can produce an ill-formed integer constant (debug assertion failure)
confirmed.detail: getModelDisjunct's fallback (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:915-927) calls TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue for skolems missing from arithModel. The liastar extension runs BEFORE sanityCheckIntegerModel (theory_arith.cpp:287-325), and collectModelValues filters integer variables with fractional simplex values into d_arithModelCacheIllTyped rather than arithModel -- i.e. the skolem is missing from arithModel precisely in the rare case its candidate value is non-integral. The fallback then reaches TheoryArithPrivate::getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith_private.cpp:1080-1097), which does mkConstRealOrInt(term.getType(), qmodel); for an Int-typed skolem with non-integral qmodel this calls mkConstInt, whose Assert(r.isIntegral()) (node_manager_template.cpp:1446-1449) aborts debug builds, and in production builds yields a CONST_INTEGER node wrapping a non-integral rational that passes the value.isConst() check and corrupts the harvested cell. For skolems entirely unknown to the simplex the path is safe (getDeltaValue throws ModelException, caught, returns null, handled at liastar_extension.cpp:920-923). Guard the fallback with a type/integrality check (e.g. reject values whose type does not match the skolem). Also note getDeltaValue's AlwaysAssert(d_qflraStatus != Result::UNKNOWN) is satisfied in this calling context (linear postCheck completed without conflict).

verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED REAL. The failure chain reproduces step-by-step from the code, and it is exclusive to the new arith-liastar-main-solver mode (the fallback is new diff code reached only via mainSolverCheckStar -> getModelDisjunct, gated at liastar_extension.cpp:405-407).

Chain: (1) liastar checkFullEffort runs with d_arithModelCache at theory_arith.cpp:292, BEFORE sanityCheckIntegerModel at line 326. (2) TheoryArithPrivate::collectModelValues (theory_arith_private.cpp:4600-4614) routes integer variables whose simplex value is non-integral into arithModelIllTyped and skips arithModel, so a termSet-collected, simplex-known enum skolem is absent from arithModel exactly when its value is fractional. (3) The new fallback (liastar_extension.cpp:915-926) then calls TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith.cpp:511-519), which misses d_arithModelCache (same map), never consults d_arithModelCacheIllTyped, and forwards to TheoryArithPrivate::getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith_private.cpp:1080-1097). getDeltaValue returns the same fractional assignment (line 4416-4419) and line 1087 calls mkConstRealOrInt(term.getType(), qmodel). (4) The skolems are Int-typed (mkDummySkolem with the lambda bound var's type, liastar_extension.cpp:855), so mkConstRealOrInt (node_manager_template.cpp:1461-1471) calls mkConstInt whose Assert(r.isIntegral()) (line 1448; Assert=AlwaysAssert under CVC5_ASSERTIONS, check.h:121-122) aborts debug builds. In non-assertion builds a CONST_INTEGER wrapping a non-integral rational is created; it passes the value.isConst() check at liastar_extension.cpp:920 and the harvested cell is computed from a non-integral point (e.g. the fractional getConst<Rational>() comparison at lines 959-961 picking GT/LT).

The reviewer's side-claims also check out: unknown-to-simplex skolems throw ModelException in getDeltaValue's default case (4488), caught (1093-1095), null returned and handled safely at 920-923; and getDeltaValue's AlwaysAssert(d_qflraStatus != UNKNOWN) holds because updateModelCache already ran collectModelValues, which AlwaysAsserts status SAT (4566).

The trigger event (linear solver assigning a fractional value to an integer variable at full effort) is rare but real -- the entire ill-typed-map + sanityCheckIntegerModel branch-and-bound machinery (with a warning message) exists precisely to handle it, and the new mode's fresh integer skolems are ordinary simplex variables subject to it. The 9 passing regression tests do not refute a rare-event crash. Only minor nitpick: "missing from arithModel precisely when non-integral" overstates slightly -- a skolem can also be missing because it is not in termSet (the benign case the fallback was written for) -- but in that case a simplex-known skolem with a fractional value hits the same assertion, so the bug stands either way. Suggested fix direction is right, though a post-hoc type check on the returned node would not catch it in production builds (the ill-formed CONST_INTEGER still has integer type); the integrality check belongs on the rational (or the fallback should bail/consult the ill-typed cache and return Node() to retry next round, deferring to sanityCheckIntegerModel's branch-and-bound).

rejected: Driver's star disjunct is frozen at emission while the guard chain is shared per lambda: stale drivers wrongly refute literals once coverage completes
isFixed-based completeness conclusion is sound only modulo driver soundness; never fires after a user push (divergence in incremental mode)
getModelDisjunct does not verify the base predicate is true under the evaluation map
Incremental push/pop desynchronizes MainEnum/d_lastDriver from the SAT solver: enumeration runs with unconstrained guards and skolems, poisoning d_lazyCones permanently
